name: TRANSFERRIN
description: Transferrin measures iron transport protein levels and evaluates iron metabolism disorders. This test assesses nutritional status, liver function, and iron deficiency or overload states.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Beckman Coulter, Roche Cobas, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: Transferrin is the main iron transport protein in blood. Normal range 200-360 mg/dL. Low levels suggest iron deficiency, malnutrition, chronic disease, or liver dysfunction. High levels indicate iron deficiency (compensatory increase) or estrogen therapy. Transferrin saturation (%) = (Iron × 100)/Transferrin. Immunoturbidimetric assay provides accurate measurement. Used in evaluation of anemia, iron overload, and nutritional assessment. Transferrin is a negative acute phase reactant, decreasing in inflammation. Critical component of iron studies panel for comprehensive iron status evaluation.
